output.reason: A 70-year-old on warfarin with head trauma yesterday now reporting bad headache and two episodes of vomiting needs immediate emergency CT imaging and possible anticoagulation reversal for suspected intracranial bleed.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. A head injury while on warfarin, with a bad headache and vomiting today, can mean bleeding inside the head that needs an urgent CT scan. Have someone drive you or call 911 — do not drive yourself. If you become drowsy, confused, weak on one side, or have a seizure, call 911 immediately.

redFlags.concern: Head trauma while anticoagulated on warfarin
redFlags.quote: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday.
Today I have a bad headache

citations.claim: Immediate non-contrast head CT is indicated after head trauma in patients on anticoagulants or over 65.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis; imaging urgency judged clinically, not a telehealth protocol.
